key_insight: CsGeBr3 hosts long-lived, one-dimensional polar chains even in its nominally cubic phase, where opposing local polarizations yield zero net polarization.
engineering_relevance: Chain-by-chain polarization reversal could inform switching models for halide-perovskite ferroelectric devices, although device performance is not established here.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials
Analysis of local polar correlations and relaxation dynamics
evidence_signal: Simulations show polar chains extending at least tens of nanometers and relaxing on nanosecond timescales—four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 intermediate.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation evidence; experimental validation of chain lengths, lifetimes, and switching behavior remains important.
paper_title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
